# Node-Tree Read Before OCR

**Decision.** Read a ride offer's fare, distance and duration from the **accessibility node tree**.
Treat optical character recognition as a fallback for apps that render offers as images — never as the
default path.

**Date.** 2026-07-02, recorded in `01-architecture.md`, the first chapter of
[[numbered-docs-chapters]].

## The reason, as written

> "**Node tree before OCR.** OCR is the expensive, fragile path. Many Android apps expose offer text as
> real `TextView` nodes, readable in microseconds with no image processing. OCR is a fallback, not the
> default."
> — Farley/docs/ocr-overlay/01-architecture.md, 2026-07-02

Three arguments in one paragraph — cost, fragility, and the observation that the data is *already
structured*. Running a recognition model over a rendering of text that the platform will hand you as a
string is work done twice, and the second copy is lossier. It is the same instinct as
[[taught-selectors-over-guessed-labels]]: prefer the value you were given to the value you inferred.

Latency is the binding constraint. An offer card carries a countdown, and the verdict has to be on
screen while it still matters.

## Alternative rejected

**OCR-first capture** via `MediaProjection` + ML Kit. Rejected on the cost and fragility above. Two
Android permissions still declared in the manifest — `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PROJECTION` and
`FOREGROUND_SERVICE` — are the fossils of that design; no code uses them. See
[[android-accessibility-service]].

## The parse bug this design still had

Structured input does not mean unambiguous input. Ride cards list the **pickup leg before the trip
leg**, so a naive first-match read scored the wrong journey:

> "`OfferNodeParser` no longer takes the *first* money/km/min match: ride cards list the pickup leg
> before the trip leg, so first-match read the deadhead as the trip."
> — Farley/docs/ocr-overlay/CHANGELOG.md, 2026-07-03

The fix: fare is the **largest** money token; with two km/min hits the first is the pickup deadhead and
the last is the trip. That distinction is precisely what {{deadhead-adjusted-net-profit}} depends on —
the bug was silently pricing the free leg as the paid one.

## Confirmed drift — OCR was never built

The README, VISION and four documents describe **Android ML Kit OCR as the shipped on-device engine**.
It is not shipped in any form:

- `com.google.mlkit:text-recognition` appears in **no** `build.gradle`.
- `OcrReader.readNow()` returns `null` behind a `// TODO(Phase 4)`.
- `OcrReader.instance` is never set, so the fallback cannot be reached even if it worked.
- `vision.ts` carries an explicit `NB (native)` note that ML Kit text still needs wiring into
  `ScreenCapture.hint`.

The working on-device reader is the node-tree parser, and the classifier that supports it runs over the
node tree's flat text — not over pixels. Confirmed at interview; recorded on [[farely]] and
[[documentation-drift]] as this repository's sharpest doc-vs-code gap. The decision itself was correct
and was simply never revisited by the prose; what drifted is the claim that the *rejected* path also
exists.
